did_you_know.text: The phrase “the windows of heaven” pictures the sky as having openings through which rain pours. Together with “the fountains of the deep,” it describes water coming both from above and from the depths.
The phrase “going and returning” emphasizes a gradual, continuing process rather than a sudden change. Even after the rain stopped, the waters receded slowly.
“The mountains of Ararat” do not necessarily mean one particular peak. They are usually associated with the ancient land of Urartu, around present-day eastern Turkey and Armenia.
The olive leaf became a symbol of hope and peace because it showed Noah that the waters had receded and plants were growing again. The olive tree was also very important in ancient cultures.
This is the first mention in the Torah of building an altar. The word “olah” is related to the verb “to rise,” because the offering was placed on the altar and burned completely.

The phrase “the Lord said in his heart” is a vivid way of describing a firm inner decision. The verse also recognizes that people tend to make mistakes from childhood, so the world needs mercy, not only punishment.
The verse presents nature’s cycles in pairs: planting and harvest, cold and heat, summer and winter, day and night. The list emphasizes that life on earth will continue according to a regular rhythm.
